Avg_GRM

Source: vignettes/articles/criterion-avggrm.Rmd
criterion-avggrm.Rmd

The mean genomic relationship between the training set and the target.

Type Relationship
Direction Larger is better
Uses a test set yes; without a test set, all candidates
Score a given set avg_grm_score()
Search with it optTrain(method = "AvgGRM")

Definition

Avg_GRM=𝟏n′GTP𝟏nP/(nnP)\mathrm{Avg\_GRM} = \mathbf{1}_n' G_{TP} \mathbf{1}_{n_P}/(n\,n_P) with G=XX′/pG = XX'/p. Without a test set, the target is the whole candidate set.

Use in TSDFGS 

library(TSDFGS)
data(geno)
avg_grm_score(geno[1:50, ], geno[51:100, ])
## [1] -0.158039
fit <- optTrain(geno, cand = 1:404, n.train = 50, method = "AvgGRM",
                 min.iter = 300, console = FALSE, seed = 1)
fit$OPTtrain
##  [1] 403 303  74 339 142  71 307  85 277 304 330  51  12 244 321  60 117 240 392
## [20] 306 302 168 216 325 300  96 154  43  65 301  20  44 320 305 121 335 260 388
## [39]  82   3 152 298  16  77  36  17 349 246 348  97
# targeted: the test set is known
fit2 <- optTrain(geno, cand = 1:300, n.train = 50, test = 301:404,
                  method = "AvgGRM", min.iter = 300, console = FALSE, seed = 1)
fit2$OPTtrain
##  [1]  77 245 143  43 215  31  88 149 116 297 185 268  52 161  27  65 283  44 168
## [20] 121  40 244  10 282 296  39 162  20  12 246 142 195  71  18  74 256 216 299
## [39]  67  17  96 189 117 126 248 277   5 221 156 101

The search is a random-start exchange (hill-climbing) search; see How the scores are computed. Use min.iter larger than 300 on real data and check fit$converged.

Original work

Fernández-González, J., Akdemir, D., & Isidro y Sánchez, J. (2023). A comparison of methods for training population optimization in genomic selection. Theoretical and Applied Genetics, 136, 30. https://doi.org/10.1007/s00122-023-04265-6

Repository or website of the original authors: Code of Fernández-González et al. (2023): github.com/TheRocinante-lab/Publications. Package TrainSel: github.com/TheRocinante-lab/TrainSel.
